title: Hearing on food service inspections and related food safety bills
summary: The Council's Health Committee held an oversight hearing on Department of Health and Mental Hygiene inspections of New York City's over 24,000 food service establishments, alongside several related bills. The bills would require photo or video evidence of violations, set nutrition standards for children's meals at chains, allow digital food protection certificates, regulate tobacco bars, require Legionella test reporting, and mandate food protection course recertification every five years. Data presented showed inspector staffing and inspection rates declined sharply around 2022-2023, with only 69.7 percent of restaurants receiving an initial inspection in Fiscal 2025 compared to 99.5 percent in Fiscal 2019.
